hangup — the controlling terminal went away; daemons read it as 'reload'
quit — Ctrl-\ at the terminal, stronger than INT
illegal instruction — the CPU refused the code
abort — the process killed itself on purpose (assert)
bus error — a bad physical memory access, often mmap trouble
floating point exception — divide by zero and friends
kill — cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored
user-defined signal 1 (default action kills — catch it or don't send it)
segmentation fault — an invalid memory reference
broken pipe — wrote to a pipe whose reader is gone
alarm clock — timer from alarm(2) or setitimer
termination request — the polite kill; catch it and clean up
stack fault on a coprocessor (Linux, rarely seen)
a child stopped or exited — read it to reap zombies
stop the process — cannot be caught, blocked, or ignored
terminal stop — Ctrl-Z at the terminal
a background process tried to read the terminal
a background process tried to write the terminal
virtual timer expired (counts CPU time, not wall time)
the window changed size — terminals and TUIs re-read it
bad system call — seccomp filters often speak this
